findings.new_signal_worth_flagging: The two lowest performers both used aggressive phonk/hardtekk, while the top 3 performers all used calmer confident/bittersweet mid-tempo (78-95bpm) tracks instead. Not enough data yet to flip the default, but worth testing more mid-tempo anthemic/bittersweet tracks in upcoming scouting rather than defaulting to aggressive phonk every time.

attribute_findings.attribute: Format reach gap: Shorts vs. long-form age-normalized views
attribute_findings.direction: Shorts reach the discovery funnel far more than long-form so far
attribute_findings.metrics: Short-form median age-normalized views ~123.7/day (n=31) vs. long-form ~5.6/day (n=8) — roughly a 20x gap. Long-form also shows 0 median likes/comments per 1,000 views so far.
attribute_findings.evidence_level_note: n=8 for long-form would floor to repeated_pattern by raw count alone, but this is explicitly downgraded to early_signal: the two formats are inherently different discovery mechanics (YouTube's Shorts shelf vs. long-form search/suggested), the channel is only ~1 week old, and there is NO per-video subscriber-attribution data available via any API to confirm which format is actually converting the subscribers the channel does have — this finding is about RAW REACH only, not confirmed subscriber value.
attribute_findings.alternative_explanations: Long-form videos may take longer to be surfaced by YouTube's recommendation system (a well-documented general pattern, not specific to this channel); the sample is tiny; long-form's real value (session watch time, monetization eligibility, returning viewers) is not something the available API can measure for a channel this new (estimated_minutes_watched is lag-nulled for nearly all current long-form uploads).
attribute_findings.recommended_action: Continue gathering data. Do NOT reduce long-form allocation on this evidence alone — the gap is real but the cause and the true subscriber-value comparison are not yet known. This is the current dominant candidate for 'what's limiting growth' and should be the first thing re-examined with a larger sample.
